subject.title: fix(state): recover from state-database corruption without a gateway restart

question: Should automatic recovery from a repaired shared state database be guaranteed after corruption from both read and write paths, or intentionally be limited to the next write?
rationale: The generic read executor is shared infrastructure, while cache eviction belongs to the state owner; choosing the callback or owner boundary defines the availability contract and should not be inferred from a write-only incident reproduction.

options.title: Cover reads and writes
options.body: Add an owner-safe read-time corruption hook that evicts the shared state handle and prove a repaired file recovers through a read path.

options.title: Scope recovery to writes
options.body: Retain the bounded write-triggered eviction but explicitly document and test that an idle or read-only gateway recovers on its next state write.

options.title: Pause for a state-access design
options.body: Defer this PR until maintainers choose a reusable owner-boundary design for query-time corruption recovery.

recommendation.title: Cover reads and writes
recommendation.body: Add an owner-safe read-time corruption hook that evicts the shared state handle and prove a repaired file recovers through a read path.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor has the most concrete incident and reproduction context in the available review evidence; a current-main owner should join the decision before landing.
